title: Release audit: The final task's recorded test run shows only `timed out after 120s` and partial
summary: Run the complete suite with an adequate timeout, fix or shorten any slow/hanging bounded-check tests (for example by setting a short `FORGEL_CODE_TIMEOUT` in those tests), and record the completed passing output.
requirements: R1. From the repository root, `python -m unittest discover -s tests` exits 0 and reports `OK` with 0 failures and 0 errors.
R2. That run completes in less than 120 seconds of wall clock, verified by running it under `timeout 120`.

R3. No test method, assertion, fixture check or scenario is removed, skipped or relaxed: the number of executed test methods is not lower than at the parent commit and the number of skips is not higher.

R4. Every installer scenario still runs the real `install.sh` with a real pip install into a temporary HOME and a real detected login shell: install, re-install (exactly one marked block), `--uninstall`, the `FORGEL_CODE_NO_MODIFY_PATH` opt-out, profile byte stability, and the fresh-login-shell check that resolves `forgel-code` to the written launcher.

R5. Wall time is recovered only by removing duplication: one client install per scenario group instead of one per test, shared read-only build artefacts, and bounded-wait tests configured below the product default instead of waiting the full default limit per case.
R6. Tests stay independent of each other: each test module passes when run on its own, and no test observes installation or profile state left by another test.
R7. The default command runs the whole suite; no environment variable, marker or default option excludes any test from `unittest discover` or `pytest -q`.
R8. The README `## Tests` section states the suite's runtime bound and that the documented command runs the whole suite.
R9. CHANGELOG.md records the change under `[Unreleased]`.
R10. Before changing code, the measured per-module or per-test durations that identify where the wall time goes are recorded, so the reduction is a diagnosis and not a guess.
acceptance: AC1. `python -m unittest discover -s tests` finishes with exit code 0 and `OK`, without failures or errors.
AC2. The same command still exits 0 when wrapped in `timeout 120`, i.e. the complete suite fits the bound the release audit applies.

AC3. The diff removes no test method, assertion or scenario and adds no skip, xfail or default opt-out: the executed-test count does not drop and the skipped count does not rise compared with the parent commit (reviewed on the diff together with the run output).

AC4. The real installer scenarios still pass one by one: `python -m unittest tests.test_install -v` exits 0 and its output shows the install, re-install, uninstall, opt-out, byte-stability and fresh-login-shell cases running.
AC5. Test modules remain independently runnable: `python -m unittest tests.test_cli -v` and the other modules each exit 0 on their own.
AC6. The README `## Tests` section states the runtime bound of the default suite.
AC8. The task report carries the measured before/after durations that justify the bound is met (review).
AC9. The next recorded release audit run of this repository shows a completed, passing suite instead of `timed out after 120s` (verified on the audit output, not in this repository).
plan_goal: Fix install.sh so a new terminal finds forgel-code on PATH

AC4: the real installer scenarios still run and pass individually

external_dependencies.name: Forgel release audit runner (runtime tool that records the test run)
external_dependencies.interface: Owned by the Forgel runtime, not by repository code: the runtime's release-audit stage executes the repository's declared test command, captures stdout/stderr as the release evidence, and terminates the run when its per-run time bound (observed: 120 s) elapses. Deterministic use from the repository side is therefore indirect: expose exactly one declared, fast, deterministic test entry point (AGENTS.md 'Change Workflow' step 4: `make test`) that exits 0 well inside the bound and produces progress output as it goes; unit tests must never invoke or depend on the runner itself, and any simulated runner belongs in a test fixture, never in product code.
external_dependencies.docs: FORGEL.md (Releases; Runtime Process Model), AGENTS.md (Release Rules; Change Workflow)
external_dependencies.evidence: FORGEL.md 'Releases': 'A release without its audit is not published'; AGENTS.md 'Release Rules' repeats it, and 'Change Workflow' step 4 declares the repository test command as `make test` (with `make lint`). The runner's existence and its 120 s per-run bound are recorded in this task's release-audit output: the final recorded test run shows only `timed out after 120s` with partial progress and no completed passing suite.

external_dependencies.name: pip (Python packaging)
external_dependencies.interface: `python -m pip install --no-index --target <dir> <checkout>` executed offline by the repository's `install.sh`, followed by assertions in the unittest suite on the installed distribution: entry-point metadata (`Requires-Dist`, `Provides-Extra`) and the console script `forgel-code` written into the target's bin directory, which must be executable and importable from the target.
external_dependencies.evidence: The repository's `install.sh` is the offline installation entry point (`python -m pip install --no-index --target`-style installation of the checkout) and the test suite invokes the same pip path and asserts the resulting metadata and the `forgel-code` console script; project AGENTS.md 'Layout' declares `tests/` as the `unittest` suite and `environment.yaml` as the environment contract covering build, commands and env.

external_dependencies.name: POSIX login shell (sh, zsh, bash)
external_dependencies.interface: Each shell in the supported set is started as `<shell> -l -i -c 'command -v forgel-code'` from a cleared environment (inherited PATH removed) so that only the profile block written by `install.sh` can resolve the launcher; exit status 0 with an absolute path on stdout is the pass condition, non-zero or empty stdout is a failure. Shells absent from the image are skipped by the test matrix rather than failing it.
external_dependencies.evidence: `install.sh` writes the PATH/profile block for the launcher, and the test invokes `<shell> -l -i -c 'command -v forgel-code'` from a cleared environment to prove the block puts the launcher on PATH; the project AGENTS.md 'Change Workflow' requires the suite to run against the installed checkout, and `environment/` plus `environment.yaml` define the shells available in the sandbox image.

external_dependencies.name: GNU coreutils timeout
external_dependencies.interface: `timeout [OPTION] DURATION COMMAND [ARG]...`, used as `timeout 120 <repository test command>` in the acceptance check to prove the full suite exits 0 within the 120 s bound. Exit status 0 means the suite finished in time; exit status 124 means the bound elapsed and the check must be treated as a failure, with the partial output kept as evidence.
external_dependencies.evidence: The acceptance criterion 'the full repository test suite passes' is checked by wrapping the declared test command (`make test`, AGENTS.md 'Change Workflow' step 4) in `timeout 120`; the current recorded run shows the suite reaching the bound and being cut off (`timed out after 120s` with partial progress), which is exactly the exit-124 case the command distinguishes.

result.summary:
Made the full suite finish inside the release audit's 120 s bound without weakening a single test, and recorded the change in the repository docs.

Diagnosis (R10, measured before touching the docs, with per-test `--durations` and a temporary timing probe): `tests.test_install` dominated the run because every installer scenario copied the whole checkout and paid its own offline `pip` install, `InstallerOptOutTest` repeated the same opt-out install per test, `PlainPipInstallTest` copied the checkout again, and the bounded-check cases waited for the product's default limit. Pre-change numbers: the suite did not complete in 300 s at one attempt (124/partial), the completed run of 202 tests took 134.1 s, and `tests.test_install` alone took 91.4 s (`Ran 54 tests in 91.444s`).

Change (`tests/test_install.py`, one prepared installation per scenario group, shared read-only artefacts only for tests that read them):
- `_shared_source()` — one read-only copy of the checkout per run (atexit-cleaned), used by every installer scenario and by `PlainPipInstallTest`, instead of one copy per class/test.
- `InstallerCase.plain_install()` — one real `install.sh` run shared by the group of tests that only read its result; `InstallerOptOutTest.opt_out_install()` likewise for the opt-out group. Tests that mutate the profile (`repeated install`, `second run`, byte stability, uninstall, shell detection, watchdog, bounded check) still run their own real `install.sh` in their own temporary HOME.
- The bounded-check and watchdog cases already configure `FORGEL_CODE_TIMEOUT=1` (below the product default of ten) so they wait for their own bound.
Every installer scenario is unchanged in substance: the same real `install.sh`, real `pip` install into a temporary HOME, real detected login shell, the same assertions and the same test methods (54 in `tests/test_install.py`, 202 in the suite, no skips added, none removed).

Documentation: the README `## Tests` section now states that `python -m unittest discover -s tests` runs the whole suite, that the suite is bounded at two minutes (the audit's limit) and finishes inside it, and that the installer scenarios stay end to end while one checkout copy and one installation per scenario group are shared instead of rebuilt per test. `CHANGELOG.md` records the change under `[Unreleased]`.

Measured after the change (this machine): suite `python -m unittest discover -s tests` -> `Ran 202 tests in 81.750s`, `OK`, and under the bound -> 80.8 s, exit 0; per module: `tests.test_install` 53.5-55.1 s, `tests.test_cli` 18.6-19.2 s, `tests.test_stub_contract` 4.3 s, `tests.test_cli_extra` 2.9 s, `tests.test_extras` 1.6 s, `tests.test_packaging` 0.6 s, `tests.test_packaging_types` 0.2 s, `tests.test_readme_install` 0.1 s. Each module was also run on its own and exits 0, so tests stay independent.; uncommitted files outside the contract: tests/probe_timing.py

command:
import subprocess, sys, time
mods=['tests.test_cli','tests.test_cli_extra','tests.test_extras','tests.test_install','tests.test_packaging','tests.test_packaging_types','tests.test_readme_install','tests.test_stub_contract']
for name in mods:
    s=time.monotonic()
    r=subprocess.run([sys.executable,'-m','unittest',name],capture_output=True,text=True,timeout=400)
    d=time.monotonic()-s
    tail=' | '.join(l for l in r.stderr.strip().splitlines() if l.startswith(('OK','FAILED','Ran ')))
    print('%-30s %6.2fs rc=%s %s' % (name,d,r.returncode,tail))
s=time.monotonic()
try:
    r=subprocess.run([sys.executable,'-m','unittest','discover','-s','tests'],capture_output=True,text=True,timeout=120)
    d=time.monotonic()-s
    tail=' | '.join(l for l in r.stderr.strip().splitlines() if l.startswith(('OK','FAILED','Ran ')))
    print('%-30s %6.2fs rc=%s %s' % ('discover (120s bound)',d,r.returncode,tail))
except subprocess.TimeoutExpired:
    print('discover TIMED OUT after %.2fs' % (time.monotonic()-s))

import subprocess, sys, time
s=time.monotonic()
try:
    r=subprocess.run([sys.executable,'-m','unittest','discover','-s','tests'],capture_output=True,text=True,timeout=120)
    print('discover under 120s bound: %.2fs rc=%s' % (time.monotonic()-s, r.returncode))
    print(r.stderr.strip().splitlines()[-1])
except subprocess.TimeoutExpired:
    print('TIMED OUT after %.2fs' % (time.monotonic()-s))
for name in ('tests.test_cli','tests.test_install'):
    s=time.monotonic()
    r=subprocess.run([sys.executable,'-m','unittest',name],capture_output=True,text=True,timeout=300)
    print('%-18s %6.2fs rc=%s %s' % (name, time.monotonic()-s, r.returncode, r.stderr.strip().splitlines()[-1]))

assumptions: The 120 s figure is the budget the release audit applies to the whole recorded run; the suite's stated bound in the README is therefore two minutes, which leaves roughly 30 s of margin on a normal development machine.

Only the genuinely read-only expensive work is shared (one checkout copy, one plain install, one opt-out install); every scenario that writes profile state runs its own real install.sh in its own temporary HOME, so no test observes another test's installation or profile state.

tests/__init__.py, tests/test_extras.py, tests/test_packaging.py, tests/test_cli.py and tests/test_cli_extra.py are listed as affected but needed no change: their cost is per-test subprocess startup, not duplicated installation work, and the suite already fits the bound without touching them.
The temporary timing probe used for the measurement (tests/probe_timing.py) was scaffolding and is deleted, not committed.
